one_line: Kerala astronomer–mathematician of the Tantrasangraha, reformer of planetary models in 15th–16th century Trikkandiyur.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, lean, scholarly build with a calm, composed posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium brown Kerala complexion, straight nose, gentle but sharp eyes, neatly trimmed black moustache, thin black eyebrows, a small sacred ash mark (vibhuti) across the forehead with a vertical sandalwood tilak in the centre; default expression is serene, focused, slightly curious.
appearance.hair: Glossy black hair gathered into a tight, modest brahmin topknot at the back crown, sides clean and tidy, no loose strands; simple off‑white cotton headband tied around the head just above the forehead, knotted at the back.
appearance.costume: Era‑accurate Nambudiri brahmin attire: a cream‑white hand‑woven cotton dhoti (mundu) wrapped from waist to ankles with a slightly thicker gold border, pleats falling in front; upper body covered in a soft off‑white cotton angavastram draped from left shoulder across chest and around back, with a faint thin gold stripe near its edge; simple wooden beaded mala around his neck, and a narrow waist cord (thread) just visible above the dhoti; bare feet in everyday setting but for the model sheet he wears plain dark brown leather sandals that keep the look modest and practical.
appearance.signature: A palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark coconut‑fiber cord in his left hand, and a thin stylus for inscribing palm leaves held delicately in his right hand.

ref_desc: Nilakantha Somayaji is a lean middle‑aged Kerala brahmin with an oval medium‑brown face, black topknot and headband, cream‑white dhoti and angavastram with gold borders, wooden mala, sandals, and a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle with stylus in a cream‑gold‑brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Nilakantha Somayaji, shown as a dignified middle‑aged Kerala brahmin scholar with a lean build and serene focused expression. His face is oval with a medium‑brown complexion, straight nose, gentle sharp eyes, thin black eyebrows, a neatly trimmed black moustache, and sacred marks: a horizontal band of vibhuti across the forehead with a vertical sandalwood tilak in the centre. His glossy black hair is gathered into a tight brahmin topknot at the back crown, encircled by a simple off‑white cotton headband tied just above the forehead and knotted at the back. He wears an era‑accurate cream‑white cotton dhoti (mundu) from waist to ankles with a slightly thicker golden‑yellow border and clean front pleats, and a matching off‑white angavastram draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back with a faint thin gold stripe along the edge, keeping his torso modestly covered. A simple wooden beaded mala hangs at his neck, and a subtle waist cord is visible above the dhoti. His feet are in plain dark brown leather sandals. In his left hand he carries a tied bundle of palm‑leaf manuscripts with visible layered leaves and a dark coconut‑fiber cord, while his right hand holds a thin stylus used for inscribing the leaves, giving an academic, astronomical aura. Use a harmonious palette of cream white for garments, golden yellow for borders and tilak, medium brown for skin, dark brown for sandals and manuscript cord, and a muted blue‑grey accent in shadows; show him front, side and back views to fix the face, topknot and headband, draped costume, sandals, and palm‑leaf bundle with stylus.
